title: Ancient Trees in the United States: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Some American cities keep real tree registers and most do not, so the famous American trees are destinations in themselves. 19 cities mapped, 149 trees.
intro: America's most famous trees are destinations rather than city sights. People drive to the Angel Oak outside Charleston and to the Hundred-Horse Chestnut's American cousins the way they drive to a canyon, and that is how this country reads on a map of old trees. The registers behind them are patchy in a way that surprised us: Portland keeps a genuine Heritage Tree list and Hawaii designates individual Exceptional Trees by county ordinance, while Philadelphia, Charleston, Seattle, San Francisco and Savannah have no curated list at all. They either protect any tree over a set trunk size automatically, or they publish every street tree they own and nothing in between. So the good American trees are found one at a time, by name, and that is how we map them.
